abstract:
We prove a shifted mean-square estimate for primitive sextic Kubota series over the Eisenstein integers. For $H_\nu(r,u)=\sum_{(c,r)=1}\nu(c)g_6(r,c)(Nc)^{-u}$, fixed local data, $0<\eta<1/12$, and good $h$, we obtain
$$
\sum_{Nn\le X}|H_\nu(hn,1+\eta+it)|^2
\ll_{\eta,\varepsilon}(Nh\,X)^\varepsilon(Nh)^{1/2}X(1+|t|)^6.
$$
The numerator columns are unrestricted. Primitive inversion produces a weighted full-series family with numerators $hab^3$. At its natural functional-equation length, the sextic sieve in $a$ and quadratic sieve in $b$ control complementary ranges. A pole-cancelling Mellin kernel permits absorption in the full fixed local Kubota vector without a residue mean or an explicit sextic theta formula. All numerator valuations, ray changes and coprimality masks are retained.

The theorem gives squared contour-error norm $\ll(UXNR)^\varepsilon X(NR)^{1/2}$ for actual adjoint Gauss images. Combining it with fixed residual theta periodicity, primitive residue density and a positive Rankin–Selberg residue proves
$$
\Theta_6(U,X)=(UX)^{o(1)}\bigl(U+X+U^{5/6}X^{1/3}+U^{1/3}X^{5/6}\bigr),
$$
in the sense of matching bounds up to arbitrary subpowers, for the sextic character operator with both indices sixth-power-free. In particular its balanced squared norm is $X^{7/6+o(1)}$. Prime inflation also gives balanced annular bounds: exponent $7/6$ for sixth-power-free indices and exponent $17/16$ for squarefree indices, the latter using Xu–Sang’s full-cutoff lower bound. We do not obtain the analogous all-range squarefree-squarefree lower bound. Under an explicit Gram hypothesis we also approximate a specified row correction by its theta-residue matrix. Finite CPU checks verify inversion algebra only. The full complementary operator on the motivating Möbius/plain coefficient remains uncontrolled; no new zero-free region or resolution of RH follows.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Address all five v1 review requests with explicit norm sums, smoothed dyadic accounting, the fixed local character vector, the nonzero translation projector, and the Wiener–Ikehara hypotheses. Add Corollary 7: a standard prime-inflation proof transfers the full-cutoff lower bounds to balanced annuli, yielding exponent 7/6 for sixth-power-free indices and 17/16 for squarefree indices from Xu–Sang. The accepted mean and all-range sixth-power-free theorem are unchanged; the finite-check supplement is unchanged. Update scoped peer CRT credit.
title: Primitive sextic Kubota means and a sharp sixth-power-free large sieve
